body.x: Sorcerics (CEO Hyeonjong Ryu) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), and conducted an interview at the AVING Media Stage inside the Seoul Pavilion during the exhibition period.

Founded in 2023, Sorcerics is a startup developing AI-based smart home solutions. The company has focused on technologies that proactively and continuously understand living spaces and user conditions in real time, delivering personalized services without requiring users to issue explicit commands.

On the strength of its accumulated capabilities and proprietary technologies, Sorcerics secured early-stage investment from domestic venture capital firms and later raised USD 1 million from South Park Commons, a Silicon Valley–based investment firm, gaining recognition in the global market.
According to the company, Sorcerics has also accelerated technological advancement after being selected for the NVIDIA Inception Program and the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ Deep Tech TIPS program.

At CES 2026, Sorcerics unveiled its next-generation smart home solution, “SOL.” Selected as a CES 2026 Innovation Award winner in the Home Appliances category, SOL is an on-device AI–based smart home hub that analyzes spaces and occupant conditions in real time using visual and audio data, then automatically controls indoor environments.
The most distinctive feature of SOL lies in its realization of a “zero-command smart home,” which stems from Sorcerics’ core research area of ambient computing technology.

While conventional solutions rely on voice commands or app-based controls, SOL combines ultra-lightweight vision AI with on-device SLAM to interpret user behavior and context in real time. For example, when the system detects a user lying down on a bed, it automatically adjusts bedroom lighting and air conditioning to optimize the sleep environment.

SOL also demonstrates strengths in privacy protection and accessibility. The device processes all data internally, minimizing concerns about personal data leakage while maximizing processing speed from data recognition to action execution. In addition, SOL supports major smart home platforms, including Samsung SmartThings and Google Home.

With SOL making its debut at CES 2026, Sorcerics plans to enter the global smart home market, starting with North America. Hyeonjong Ryu, CEO of Sorcerics, said, “Our SOL, which offers differentiated proactivity while eliminating concerns over personal data leakage, embodies the key characteristics required of next-generation smart homes in the global market.” He added, “North America in particular represents one of the regions with the highest demand for smart home technologies, making it an ideal stage for Sorcerics to expand global partnerships and pursue localization strategies.”

Ryu continued, “Building on the global buyer network secured at CES, we aim to expand distribution channels while continuously developing features tailored to local consumers, ultimately positioning SOL as a next-generation standard in the smart home sector.”

body.x: The company participated in CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026 supported a total of 70 startups with participation from 19 startup support organizations based in Seoul, including the Seoul Business Agency, district offices, related institutions, and universities. The 70 exhibiting companies were composed of startups offering products and services based on advanced technologies such as AI, mobility, and healthcare. Among them, selected outstanding companies were given the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled.
